docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Overview

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Physical education is a central component of the curriculum and enhances school education by adding a physical and motor dimension. It supports the development of students by strengthening motor skills, body awareness, self-confidence, as well as social and emotional competencies. Students gain a wide range of movement experiences, explore various forms of physical activity and play, and are empowered to participate actively, fairly, and reflectively in sports and movement culture. Physical education not only focuses on performance development but also emphasizes the joy of movement, the promotion of teamwork, and respectful interaction.

docs.title: Competences
docs.text:
Every movement involves both control and energy, working together to create coordinated actions. To support effective movement learning, it's essential to develop body awareness, coordination skills, and physical fitness. These foundational elements are integrated across all areas of the physical education curriculum. The following six competence areas highlight how these aspects are addressed and developed through physical activity:

Running, Jumping, Throwing Moving on Gymnastic Equipment

Performing and Dancing Playing Sliding, Rolling, Riding

Moving in Water

docs.title: Cycles
docs.text:
The school years in Switzerland are divided into 3 different cycles. The first cycle includes kindergarten till 2nd grade. The second cycle is from 3rd grade till 6th grade and the third cycle contains 7th, 8th and 9th grade. The curriculum in PE is also divided into these 3 cycles.

Warning

The teachers cycle and the curriculum cycle do not line up. A teacher is normally for 2 years with the class: first two years of kindergarten, 1st - 2nd grade, 3rd - 4th grade, 5th - 6th grade and 7th - 9th grade. Therefore, it is difficult to cover all the competences, and proper communication when handing over the class to the next teacher is key.

First Cycle Second Cycle Third Cycle

docs.title: Focus Area
docs.text:
I’ve focused on receiving and passing, which is a key component of the playing competence. Since I mostly teach 3rd-grade PE classes, my focus has primarily been on the second cycle. However, as the 3rd grade has just entered the second cycle, it is also important to consider some elements from the first cycle.

Focus Area

docs.title: Focus Area
docs.text:
Focus Area

The competence area “Playing” is further divided into Movement Games, Sport Games and Combat Games. Each of these areas includes several subcategories. I have chosen to focus on receiving and passing, which is part of the Sport Games category. I selected this focus because I believe it is important in many ways and frequently used in everyday life. It helps students not only to participate in games, but also supports their motor, cognitive, social, and emotional development.

Focusing on receiving and passing will support my development as a coach because it challenges me to work with a wide range of abilities. Some students are still developing basic motor skills, while others are quite advanced. This forces me to adapt my teaching, try different strategies, and learn what works best. It helps me build key coaching skills like adapting, differentiating, planning, and making decisions in real time.

As I am currently teaching a 3rd grade PE class, I have chosen to focus specifically on the second cycle. However, it is important not to look at one cycle in isolation. The other cycles must always be considered as well. In my case, the first cycle is especially relevant, as my 3rd grade class has just entered the second cycle. This means that some basic requirements from the first cycle still need to be addressed before moving forward.

Think outside the box

The various competence areas and their subcategories often share similarities and intersect with one another. These connections should be taken into account when planning and implementing lessons.

docs.title: Demands of different Cycles
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Receive and pass objects
    • Receive and pass a ball or other game object while running
    • Keep the ball or game object in play in small group situations
  • Second Cycle:
    • Receive and pass the ball or game object in small team games
    • Receive and pass the ball or game object in simplified team sports
  • Third Cycle:
    • Receive and pass the ball or game object appropriately in game situations

docs.title: First Cycle
docs.text:
Receive and pass objects:

  • Groups of two, passing all different kind of objects, vary the distance between them, vary way how to pass (bounce off the floor, bounce of the wall, two hands, one hand, foot, sticks)
  • Working alone with a ball (throwing in the air catching again, make it more difficult e.g clapping between, spin)

Receive and pass a ball or other game object while running:

  • Pairs are running from one side of the hall to the other while passing an object (variation: bouncing off the floor, change speed of running, use two hands, one hand, foot, sticks)

Keep the ball or game object in play in small group situations:

  • Passing in small groups with a certain goal (e.g. ball isn't allowed to touch the floor, passing 10 times without a misplaced pass)
  • Rope ball (simplified volleyball where catching is allowed)
  • Hoop touch down (simplified rugby, not allowed to walk with the ball, team tries to touch down the ball in the hoop, different varietions e.g. several hoops, different field sizes, different balls)

docs.title: Second Cycle
docs.text:
Receive and pass the ball or game object in small team games:

  • Passing game (small teams, which team reaches first 10 passes without getting interupted from the other team)
  • Monkey in the middle (kids learn to pass while getting some pressure)
  • Relays
  • Students are in a circle, two balls, pass to every second student, can one ball overtake the other
  • Line ball (simplified rugby, touch down behind a certain line, only 3 steps with the ball)

Receive and pass the ball or game object in simplified team sports:

  • Floorball (but with less rules)
  • Bench Soccer
  • Dice Floorball or Soccer (the number rolled determines how many players enter the field)
  • Simplified volleyball (use a bench instead of a net or a lower net, ball is allowed to bounce off the floor once)
  • Basketball with adapted rules (e.g. kids aren't allowed to walk with the ball, lower the basket)
  • Playing team sports but adapting rules, field size and group size

docs.title: Third Cycle
docs.text:
Receive and pass the ball or game object appropriately in game situations:

  • Play team games with normal rules (e.g. floorball, soccer, volleyball, basketball, ultimate, baseball, touch rugby, badminton)
  • Invent extra rules (e.g. number of passes required before scorring is allowed)

docs.title: General activities
docs.text:
Kids often first need to learn how to throw and how to catch before they can play games with receiving and passing. Throwing is also part of the competence "Running, Jumping, Throwing". As described earlier the competences often overlap. Activities that help the students to learn how to throw:

  • Throwing tennis balls with guidance
  • Throwing tennis balls with a target (e.g. through a hoop, in a box, throw done cones)
  • Two teams are positioned on opposite sides of the hall. Three large balls are placed in the middle. Students throw tennis balls from their side, trying to hit the large balls and roll them over to the opponents' side.
  • Dodgeball (students love this game, they need to throw precise and if they catch the ball they save themselves.)
  • Brennball (simplified baseball), one team needs to throw and opposite team tries to catch to get some points as well

docs.title: Difficulties
docs.text:
Difference in skill levels:

A class normally has around 20 students. Skill levels as well as motivation levels often vary widely. The gap in skill levels often results in only the more skilled students throwing and catching during games, and they tend to pass mostly to other skilled students. As a result, lower-skilled students rarely receive the game object, which means they have fewer opportunities to improve their skills, which makes the gap even bigger.

Tip

Keep this in mind when planning activities and adapt them in a way that ensures all students are involved so that everyone receives and makes passes.

Some Strategies/Activities to address this:

  • Group composition (e.g. pairs of a better skilled with a lower skilled)
  • Dividing class (pay attention to not discriminate someone)
  • Specific game rules (everyone from the team needs to have the game objects before scoring is allowed, girls score counts double)
  • Relays

Fear of balls:

A lot of younger students are scared of balls. It is important to address this and help them overcome their fear.

Some Strategies/Activities to address this:

  • Using softballs (this shows them that it does not hurt)
  • Building up self-confidence (helps them to catch balls)
  • Encourage them from outside
  • Starting with small games where they don't get hit
  • Working/playing with balls often

docs.title: Techniques
docs.text:
In this section we briefly cover the techniques of receiving and passing.

Receiving:

  • Body position:
    • Body position depends on passing style and game objects. But you should always be ready to receive the pass (e.g. hands out of pockets, looking where your teammate with the game object is)
    • Show and teach the kids the differences (e.g. floorball: holding stick in both hands and stay deep, soccer: standing on the leg that is not stopping the pass, dodgeball: having the hands ready in front of the body)
  • Moving towards the pass:
    • To receive a pass it is important to move towards it and not stand still or go in another direction
    • There are exeptions e.g. if a pass is played into the run
  • Getting open to provide a good passing option:
    • To receive a pass you need to be free and not marked by an opponent
    • Running a way from the opponents, trying to have a direct open line to teammate with the game object
    • Talking together and tell if you are ready for the pass or not

Passing:

  • Body position:
    • Body position depends on passing style and game objects. But your head should be up and your should have some body tension (for some games more than others depending on how much body contact is allowed)
    • Show and teach the kids the differences (e.g. floorball: holding stick in both hands and stay deep, soccer: standing on the leg that is not kicking the ball and place the ball correctly, dodgeball: having the ball in one hand, throwing over the head)
  • Deciding where to pass:
    • Keep your head up (look out for teammates and opponents)
    • Talking together
  • Passing precise:
    • Look at the spot where you want to pass
    • Regulate the force you put into the pass

docs.title: Impact as a Teacher
docs.text:
• Praise the students (encourage lower skilled students)

  • Demonstrations (show them how to do it, but also let them show it to each other)

  • Giving a lot of feedback (group and individual)

  • Influence the group dynamic (avoid making fun of each other, often change groups, help building a supportive and secure learning environment)

  • Goal setting (In the 2nd cycle of PE, every student should be able to reach the goals, therefore, the goal setting process is very important. Maybe even include them in this process and use a self-assess approach)

docs.text:

docs.title: Moving in Water
docs.text:
Moving in Water

The students are able to assess situations in, on, and around water in terms of safety and behave appropriately. The focus is on swimming safely. In addition to learning swimming techniques, they acquire selected competencies in other aquatic activities such as diving, underwater swimming, and lifesaving.

docs.title: Swimming
docs.text: The students can swim safely. They know technical characteristics of different swimming techniques and apply them.

docs.title: Swimming
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Move and play freely in chest-deep water
    • Apply the core elements of breathing, floating, gliding, and propulsion in various situations
    • Stay afloat in place for one minute
  • Second Cycle:
    • Swim 50 meters in a self-chosen technique
    • Apply core movements of back crawl and front crawl
    • Apply core movements of breaststroke
    • Name and apply key features of one alternating and one simultaneous stroke over 50 meters
  • Third Cycle:
    • Swim 100 meters in a self-chosen technique
    • Swim a long distance using a freely chosen technique
    • Name and apply key features of various swimming techniques
    • Apply techniques from other aquatic sports

docs.title: Jumping into Water and Diving
docs.text: The students can jump into the water feet- and head-first and dive.

docs.title: Jumping into Water and Diving
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Jump feet-first into chest-deep water
    • Stay underwater briefly and exhale while submerged
    • Jump into deep water and submerge completely
    • Keep their eyes open underwater and retrieve objects in chest-deep water
  • Second Cycle:
    • Roll into deep water
    • Dive a short distance with few strokes
  • Third Cycle:
    • Dive head-first into deep water and reach a depth greater than their height
    • Perform various jumps from different heights
    • Equalize pressure when diving to depth

docs.title: Security in the Water
docs.text: The students can assess situations in, near, and on the water with regard to safety and act responsibly in dangerous situations.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Name risks in, near, and on the water
    • Recognize dangerous situations and follow rules under supervision
  • Second Cycle:
    • Realistically assess and avoid dangerous situations
    • Follow swimming and diving safety rules
    • Act responsibly in dangerous situations
  • Third Cycle:
    • Remind others to follow swimming and diving safety rules
    • Act responsibly toward themselves and others
    • Name causes of drowning

docs.title: Alarming and Rescuing
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Raise the alarm on instruction
  • Second Cycle:
    • Recognize when a person is in distress and raise the alarm
  • Third Cycle:
    • Recognize emergencies and take appropriate action
    • Apply basic rescue techniques

docs.title: Moving on Gymnastic Equipment
docs.text:
Moving on Gymnastic Equipment

The students gain experience in dealing with gravity and improve their strength and flexibility. They expand their movement repertoire using various gymnastic equipment and learn to perform movements in a coordinated and harmonious way. The students learn to assess risks and overcome fears. Collaborative movement activities, as well as assisting and ensuring safety, contribute to the development of their cooperation skills.

docs.title: Basic Movements on Gymnastic Equipment
docs.text: The students can perform basic movement such as balancing, rolling-turning, swinging, jumping, supporting, and climbing responsibly. They know the quality criteria and are able to assist and ensure safety for one another.

docs.title: Balance
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Balance on a narrow surface
    • Balance on a narrow surface in various ways
    • Balance on unstable equipment
  • Second Cycle:
    • Balance on equipment under challenging conditions
    • Perform a sequence of movements for balancing
  • Third Cycle:
    • Balance on difficult and challenging equipment

docs.title: Rolling and Turning
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Roll and turn on an inclined Surface
    • Perform a forward roll
    • Roll and turn on various apparatus
  • Second Cycle:
    • Perform rolling and turning movements
    • Perform a sequence of rolling and turning movements
  • Third Cycle:
    • Perform rolling and turning movements under challenging conditions
    • Perform rolling or turning movements with a flight phase in a controlled manner

docs.title: Swinging
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Swing on and off different pieces of equipment
    • Perceive the turning point during swinging and pendulum movements
    • Swing rhythmically on the rings
  • Second Cycle:
    • Enhance swinging movements by adding elements
  • Third Cycle:
    • Perform a sequence of swinging or pendulum movements.
    • Perform a sequence of movements under challenging conditions

docs.title: Springing, Supporting and Climbing
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Move on apparatus by supporting themselves and swinging
    • Land with control
    • Jump off a springboard with both feet and land with control
    • Overcome various obstacles in a sequence by supporting themselves and climbing
  • Second Cycle:
    • Jump powerfully off the springboard, perform movements in the air, and land with control
    • Efficiently overcome a sequence of obstacles
  • Third Cycle:
    • Vary the way of overcoming obstacles
    • Perform overhead support jumps

docs.title: Risk and Responsibility
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Recognize risky situations and name the emotions
    • Reflect on risky situations with guidance
  • Second Cycle:
    • Realistically assess themselves in risky situations
    • Act responsibly in risky situations
  • Third Cycle:
    • Act responsibly towards others and themselves

docs.title: Supporting, Securing and Cooperating
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Lead each other
    • Carry each other correctly and safely
    • Name equipment, transport it correctly, and set it up according to a plan
  • Second Cycle:
    • Help and spot each other during movement tasks
    • Apply spotting techniques and safety measures appropriately to the situation
  • Third Cycle:
    • Create and present movement sequences on apparatus combinations in groups

docs.title: Flexibility, Strength and Bodytension
docs.text: The students can build body tension, support their body, and move their joints through a functional range of motion. They know how to train flexibility and strength.

docs.title: Flexibilty and Strength
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Perceive the range of motion of their joints
    • Utilize the range of motion of their joints and support their body
    • Support their tense body on their hands
  • Second Cycle:
    • Maintain and improve flexibility and strength under guidance
  • Third Cycle:
    • Explain and apply training principles for improving flexibility and increasing strength
    • Independently train flexibility and strength

docs.title: Body Tension
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Perceive the body as relaxed and tense
    • Tense the body in static I-poses
  • Second Cycle:
    • Purposefully apply the core poses in movement
  • Third Cycle:
    • Tense and relax their body at the right moments during movement sequences

docs.title: Performing and Dancing
docs.text:
Performing and Dancing

The students are able to move in harmony with rhythm and music, enhancing their perception. They expand and deepen their abilities in rhythm, creative movement, and expression, and they can perform movement arts using various materials. A respectful attitude toward themselves and others fosters constructive group dynamics. They learn to present themselves confidently through performances.

docs.title: Body Awareness
docs.text: The students can perceive their body, control it deliberately, and correct themselves during movement execution.

docs.title: Body Awareness
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Perceive the environment and themselves using various senses and distinguish and name body parts
    • Perceive the position of the body in space
    • Deliberately control body parts
  • Second Cycle:
    • Understand and follow movement instructions
    • Isolate and control movements of individual body parts
    • Pay attention to the quality of movement and posture
  • Third Cycle:
    • Feel themselves during movement execution and make corrections
    • Develop an understanding of the connection between control and movement quality

docs.title: Performing and Creating
docs.text: The students can express themselves with their body and materials, choreograph a movement sequence, and present it.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Move to songs, verses, and images, and creatively interpret their content through improvisation
    • Imitate movements and experience themselves in different roles
    • Express feelings and find own movements to match them
  • Second Cycle:
    • Combine movements and design them expressively
    • Vary and design a movement sequence according to the criteria of space, time, and energy
  • Third Cycle:
    • Choreograph and present a movement sequence

docs.title: Movement Skills
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Move an object according to its properties
    • Throw and catch an object with both the right and left hand
    • Perform movement patterns using various materials
  • Second Cycle:
    • Perform movement tricks with materials
    • Perform a sequence of movement tricks
  • Third Cycle:
    • Choreograph and present a sequence of movement tricks
    • Teach movement tricks

docs.title: Dancing
docs.text: The students can recognize movement patterns, design and reproduce movement sequences and dances to music rhytmically. The treat each other with respect.

docs.title: Rhytmical Movement
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Adapt their movements to the music
    • Move with the beat
  • Second Cycle:
    • Move rhythmically to accented music
  • Third Cycle:
    • Interpret different time signatures and musical styles rhythmically
    • Recognize the structure of music and create their own movement sequence accordingly

docs.title: Dancing
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Move in contrasting ways
    • Move expressively in various dance styles
  • Second Cycle:
    • Perform dance-specific movements considering spatial pathways
    • Combine dance-specific movement patterns into movement sequences and perform them
    • Recognize and dance movement patterns from various dance styles
  • Third Cycle:
    • Memorize and present dance choreographies
    • Use the body as a means of expression, performance, and communication

docs.title: Respectful Behaviour
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Move in a group and behave respectfully
    • Appreciate the own movement expression
  • Second Cycle:
    • Respectfully acknowledge the movement expression of others
  • Third Cycle:
    • Interact respectfully during creative processes

docs.title: Playing
docs.text:
Playing

Through playful activities, the students experience joy and excitement in playing. They explore a variety of games, develop their own game ideas and agree on rules for playing together. The learn to cope with winning and losing. In both cooperative and competitive settings, students improve tactical and technical skills that are applicable across different types of games or sports. Through competition, they learn to follow established rules and rituals and to show respect for others. These situations provide opportunities to address emotional awareness, strengthen conflict resolution skills, and promote aspects of fair play.

docs.title: Movement Games
docs.text: Students can play, further develop, and invent games by making and following agreements together.

docs.title: Playing, Developing and Inventing
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Recognize given roles in games
    • Participate in games in various roles and follow the rules
    • Take on different roles during a game and act accordingly
  • Second Cycle:
    • Modify games in terms of rules, playing field, game object, team, and roles, and play independently
    • Recognize and point out fair behavior and rule violations in themselves and others
  • Third Cycle:
    • Further develop, invent, and play games independently and fairly
    • Address and resolve conflicts in games constructively

docs.title: Sport Games
docs.text: The students can apply technical and tactical action patterns in various sports. They know the rules, can play independently and fairly, and reflect on emotions.

docs.title: Receiving and Passing
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Receive and pass objects
    • Receive and pass a ball or other game object while running
    • Keep the ball or game object in play in small group situations
  • Second Cycle Focus Area:
    • Receive and pass the ball or game object in small team games
    • Receive and pass the ball or game object in simplified team sports
  • Third Cycle:
    • Receive and pass the ball or game object appropriately in game situations

docs.title: Leading Balls or Objects
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Control the ball or game object
    • Control the ball or game object next to others
  • Second Cycle:
    • Control the ball or game object in small games
  • Third Cycle:
    • Control the ball or game object effectively in team sports
    • Dribble the ball or game object and use feints

docs.title: Target Aiming
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Hit a target from a standing position
    • Hit a target while running
  • Second Cycle:
    • Hit a target during a game
  • Third Cycle:
    • Hit a target despite pressure from opponents

docs.title: Tactics
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Recognize the movements of teammates and opponents and respond accordingly
    • Offer as a passing option and pass to teammates
  • Second Cycle:
    • Recognize the path of the ball or object and identify open space
    • Position correctly in defense and protect open space
  • Third Cycle:
    • Apply tactical action patterns in team sports
    • Analyze game situations and find solutions

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Name rules
    • Follow rules
    • Apply rules while playing in small groups
  • Second Cycle:
    • Respect teammates and opponents and play without a referee for short periods
  • Third Cycle:
    • Explain important rules of sports, play independently and fairly
    • Address and resolve conflicts during play

docs.title: Emotions
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Perceive own emotions
    • Express own emotions and recognize the emotions of others
  • Second Cycle:
    • Reflect on emotions with guidance
    • Control emotions
  • Third Cycle:
    • Reflect on emotions independently
    • Manage emotions consciously

docs.title: Combat Games
docs.text: The students can fight skillfully, strategically, and fairly.

docs.title: Combat
docs.text:
• Second Cycle:
    • Deliberately throw their opponent off balance
    • Perceive and respond to the opponent’s movements in combat games
    • Roll forwards and backwards to avoid injuries
  • Third Cycle:
    • Use strength and strategy purposefully in combat games

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Accept physical contact
    • Recognize and set stop signals
    • Name and follow rituals and rules in combat games
  • Second Cycle:
    • Respect the opponent in combat games
    • Name dangerous actions and refrain from using them
  • Third Cycle:
    • Fight fairly without a referee and without injuring the opponent

docs.title: Running Jumping Throwing
docs.text:
Running, Jumping, Throwing

The students develop basic skills in running, jumping, and throwing into athletic disciplines. They practice sprinting and long-distance running, running over obstacles, and cross-country running. They learn to jump wide and high, as well as to throw and push objects far and target. They observe their progress and reflect on their personal abilities and limitations.

docs.title: Running
docs.text: The students are able to run fast, rhythmically, over obstacles, for long distances, and with spatial orientation. They know the key factors that influence performance and understand how to improve their running abilities.

docs.title: Fast Running
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Fast running
    • Run fast on the balls of the feet
    • Start from different positions and run on max speed for short distance
  • Second Cycle:
    • Identify and apply important features of sprinting technique
    • Run fast on the balls of the feet over low obstacles
  • Third Cycle:
    • Run fast and rhytmic on the balls of the feet over obstacles
    • Apply important features of sprinting techniques when running hurdles

docs.title: Endurance Running
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Recognize the own effort and rest periods
    • Run intensely again after short recovery breaks
    • Describe how effort and recovery feel in the body after intense running
  • Second Cycle:
    • Adjust their running speed during a prolonged run
    • Run for as many minutes as their age and understand that regular training is crucial for improving performance
  • Third Cycle:
    • Run for as many minutes as their age. They can explain how endurance is trained and understand the processes that occur in the body
    • Explain and perform different endurance training methods and justify their performance development

docs.title: Orientation
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Navigate independently in the gymnasium and on the school playground
    • Orient while running on the school grounds
    • Navigate while running using orientation aids
  • Second Cycle:
    • Navigate the school grounds while running using a map
    • Navigate in the school community while running using a map
  • Third Cycle:
    • Follow a route using a map in terrain or forest areas
    • Explain what to pay attention to when using a map for navigation and apply this knowledge in orienteering

docs.title: Jumping
docs.text: The students can jump in various ways, both far and high. They know the key factors that influence performance and can realistically assess their own abilities.

docs.title: Rhytmical Jumping
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Hop rhythmically
    • Perform various hopping and jumping styles using equipment/materials
    • Jump rope
  • Second Cycle:
    • Perform various tricks with the jump rope
  • Third Cycle:
    • Combine different hopping and jumping sequences, both with and without equipment
    • Teach jumps and tricks to classmates

docs.title: Long Jumping
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Jump for distance on one leg and both legs
    • Take off with the right and left leg when running up
  • Second Cycle:
    • Cover a distance using multiple jumps
    • Identify key elements of long jump technique and perform take-offs and jumps for distance using both the right and left leg
    • Convert their approach speed into a long jump
  • Third Cycle:
    • Apply key elements of long jump technique
    • Observe key elements of long jump technique in classmates and provide feedback

docs.title: High Jumping
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Jump vertically on one leg and both legs
    • Run up and jump over low obstacles using both the right and left leg for take-off
  • Second Cycle:
    • Jump vertically with an upright torso and a clear swinging leg action, taking off with both the right and left leg
    • Identify key elements of vertical jumping, take off with both the right and left leg, and perform a high jump technique
  • Third Cycle:
    • Apply key elements of a high jump technique and realistically assess their own performance
    • Observe key elements of high jump technique in their classmates and provide feedback

docs.title: Throwing
docs.text: The students can throw, push, and hurl objects over long distances and know the key factors that influence performance.

docs.title: Throwing
docs.text:
• First Cycle:
    • Throw objects far
    • Throw objects far with both the right and left hand
  • Second Cycle:
    • Identify and aplly key elements of the throwing technique with a three-step run-up
    • Perform a sling throw from a standing position
  • Third Cycle:
    • Identify and aplly key elements of the throwing technique with a five-step run-up
    • Hurl an object using a rotational movement
    • Observe key elements of throwing and hurling in classmates and provide feedback
    • Identify and aplly key elements of javelin throwing or rotational throwing

docs.title: Pushing
docs.text:
• Third Cycle:
    • Push an object for distance using full-body extension
    • Identify key elements of shot put technique and apply them during the push
    • Push a shot put far and observe key technique elements in classmates and provide feedback

docs.title: Sliding Rolling Riding
docs.text:
Sliding, Rolling, Riding

The students expand their skills in gliding, rolling, and riding, which particularly enhances their sense of balance. Depending on local conditions, they gain experience on bicycles, inline skates, ice skates, skis or snowboards. The skills and abilities they acquire can be transferred to extracurricular sports activities. Aspects of safety and sustainability are promoted, encouraging a responsible approach to both people and nature.

docs.title: Sliding, Rolling and Riding
docs.text: The students can slide, roll, and ride responsibly on various surfaces.
